Top projects include 'microsoft/markitdown' (11,962 weekly stars) for converting files to Markdown for LLMs, 'chopratejas/headroom' (1,868 weekly stars) which provides an MCP server for token-efficient RAG, 'mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills' (4,330 weekly stars) offering structured agent skills, 'anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins' (3,981 weekly stars) for agentic knowledge workflows, 'microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit' (1,529 weekly stars) for agent safety, and 'anthropics/claude-code' (3,004 weekly stars) for terminal-based agentic coding.

In the Rust ecosystem, momentum is concentrated in high-performance developer tools and agentic infrastructure. Key projects include 'Hmbown/CodeWhale' (35,709 monthly stars) for terminal-based agentic coding, 'farion1231/cc-switch' (31,143 monthly stars) as a desktop assistant for various agentic CLIs, 'openai/codex' (8,651 monthly stars) for terminal-based coding agents, '1jehuang/jcode' (4,681 monthly stars) for agent harnesses, 'xingkongliang/skills-manager' (859 monthly stars) for managing agent skills across tools, and 'ryoppippi/ccusage' (1,751 monthly stars) for tracking agent token costs.

questions about popular or trending repositories.

Your tool surface is ONE MCP tool: `fetch_url(url)`. Use it. Do not narrate;
do not invent other tools.

Procedure:
  1. Read the specific sub-question/task from the INPUTS list (look at the first literal value). If no specific task is in the INPUTS, read the overall USER_QUERY. Infer the time window (`daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`, default `weekly`) and language filter if one is mentioned.
  2. Fetch the trending page:
     `https://github.com/trending/<language>?since=<window>`
     (omit `/<language>` if none was mentioned).
  3. Extract the top 5–10 repos: name (owner/repo), description, total stars, stars gained (or weekly/monthly stars depending on the window), and URL. In your `findings`, list each repo clearly with its description, total stars, and stars gained so that downstream nodes can extract these fields.

Time budget: keep tool calls to 3 max. Do not retry a thin fetch beyond the
one fallback above.

  {
    "question": "<the question this run answered>",
    "sources": [{"url": "<url>", "title": "<title>"}, ...],
    "findings": "<2–6 short paragraphs of normalised text>"
  }

formatter does that. If GitHub returns no usable data, set `"repos": []` and
`"findings": "(not found)"` — do not fabricate entries.
